title: The Black Hole Photo Wasn't Really a Photo
hook: The iconic orange ring of the first black hole image wasn't captured — it was built from noisy data through countless judgment calls, and the real evidence is that reasonable choices all agree.
key_points: In 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of a black hole's shadow.
The underlying radio data was extremely noisy and sparse, allowing countless plausible renderings.
At every stage — including color — researchers had to choose one approach or average several.
The paper studies both 'epistemic' (valid evidence) and 'aesthetic' (visual appeal) choices made.
Different reasonable processing choices largely converge on a similar ring shape.
The authors argue that convergence, not the single famous image, is the real scientific evidence.
content_html: In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration released the now-iconic image of a black hole's shadow — a fuzzy orange ring that became an instant scientific icon. But according to a new paper on the making of that image, the picture wasn't so much captured as constructed: the underlying radio data was so noisy and sparse that countless different renderings were equally plausible.
extra_html: The authors — Rodrigo Ochigame, Emilie Skulberg, and Jeroen van Dongen — trace the choices researchers made at every stage of turning that data into a picture, including color, distinguishing "epistemic" choices (what counts as valid evidence) from "aesthetic" ones (what looks convincing). They recreate what the image would have looked like under different reasonable processing choices. Their conclusion: the single famous image isn't really the most valuable output. What matters is that many different reasonable choices converge on a similar ring — that convergence, not any one rendering, is what should count as the real result.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.
